selection: Eleven USGS parameter-00054 sites ruled new by the 2026-08-22 review of nwis-review.csv. Re-audited with tools/audit_usgs_stations.py on 2026-08-28: seven remain admitted on confirmed dam matches and three remain held with current findings under admission.py's shared screens; Topaz Lake was admitted on 2026-09-04 under ADR-110's reviewed water report without an inventory record.

review.why: The National Inventory of Dams has no record within the matching radius, and ADR-110 accepts a reviewed water report in its place: USGS defines the 32400 series as 59,440 acre-feet of usable storage between the lowest practical outlet-tunnel diversion and a level three feet below the levee crest, the Natural Resources Conservation Service independently publishes 59.4 thousand acre-feet, and the Walker River Irrigation District names Topaz as one of the two storage reservoirs it operates. The published point is the USGS site (NAD83), which NHDPlus HR resolves to exactly one waterbody within 100 metres -- GNIS Topaz Lake, 00861754, 7.5 square kilometres -- and Esri's water bodies agree, the probe's strongest outcome (ADR-106). The daily 32400 statistic runs from 1987-10-01, so the 1991-2020 normal is buildable; it needs the repository's USGS key, so it is built in CI.

capacity.capacity_source: U.S. Geological Survey water-data report, California, water year 1998, volume 3
capacity.capacity_semantics: Usable storage, 59,440 acre-feet, between the lowest practical diversion through the outlet tunnel and a level three feet below the crest of the earthfill levee, on the same basis as the reported storage series.
capacity.nid_match_finding: Searched the National Inventory of Dams within the shared matching radius of the USGS site on 2026-08-28 and again on 2026-09-04; no record corresponds. The impoundment is a natural lake raised by an outlet tunnel and levee rather than a dam the inventory lists.
capacity.controlled_works: An outlet tunnel and an earthfill levee, operated for irrigation storage by the Walker River Irrigation District.

withheld.10288500: Walker Lake. The current audit found 5,899 accepted readings since 2015 and a highest reading of 1,402,000 acre-feet. ADR-112 now permits this natural terminal lake as a separate type with no capacity, percent full, dam point or reservoir-rollup membership; held until that typed payload and closed-basin geography are implemented.
withheld.10348800: Little Washoe Lake. The current audit again found zero accepted daily readings since 2015 -- being listed by NWIS is not reporting (the Bon Tempe rule).
withheld.13087900: Milner Lake. The current audit found 4,255 accepted readings and a highest reading of 45,860 acre-feet against the matched Milner Dam-Middle record's largest pool of 39,000. The matched diversion structure's record cannot contain the observed series, and no reviewed larger full level was found. Held under the no-repair rule.
